Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: The plan provides a comprehensive district-wide inventory including detailed information on school buildings, classrooms, and other facilities such as athletic fields and cafeterias (Ch. 3-9). It includes robust condition assessments covering HVAC, plumbing, roofs, electrical, lighting, and technology infrastructure, with references to facility age and system replacements (Ch. 9-10). The plan connects facility conditions to student outcomes and instructional priorities, identifying immediate and long-term needs integrated into capital planning (Ch. 9-10, 25-27).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: The plan includes comprehensive enrollment projections with detailed methodology and assumptions, showing growth trends and capacity utilization by site and grade (Ch. 7-8, 18-21). It identifies schools nearing or at capacity and discusses specific strategies such as new school construction, boundary modifications, and interim housing (Ch. 8, 92-95, 106). The plan proposes adaptive uses of space and innovative solutions linked to enrollment data (Ch. 92-95, 106).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle, with detailed integration of district mission, instructional priorities, and facilities planning (Ch. 1-2, 22-23). The plan includes comprehensive educational specifications addressing STEM labs, collaborative spaces, special education, and career pathways (Ch. 12-13, 22-23). Facility projects are directly connected to educational goals, such as technology-rich environments and inclusive design (Ch. 12-13, 22-23).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: The plan provides data and analysis on outdoor spaces including surface types, shade coverage, and green space at multiple sites (Ch. 9-10, 14-15). It identifies strategies for campus greening such as shade structures, synthetic turf, and sustainable landscaping (Ch. 9-10, 14-15). Outdoor learning and wellness connections are mentioned at certain sites but not fully districtwide or detailed (Ch. 9-10, 14-15).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: The plan acknowledges climate-related risks such as heat and drought and includes some mitigation strategies like solar shade structures and stormwater management at specific sites (Ch. 9, 14, 16). However, it lacks a comprehensive district-wide climate risk assessment or detailed multi-risk mitigation strategies integrated into long-range planning (no explicit multi-impact climate risk assessment found).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: The plan discusses energy efficiency strategies including solar shade structures, HVAC upgrades, and installation of solar photovoltaic arrays (Ch. 9, 14, 16). It references energy resilience goals and some renewable energy integration but does not present a fully comprehensive energy resilience or electrification strategy district-wide (Ch. 9, 16). State requirements such as Title 24 and Zero Net Energy goals are mentioned (Ch. 16).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: The plan presents a comprehensive capital strategy with detailed cost estimates for all projects, including site improvements, building upgrades, and new facilities (Ch. 11, 24, 104). It outlines a clear prioritization framework and multiple funding sources including local bonds, state programs, and developer fees (Ch. 4-6, 11, 24). Long-term financial sustainability considerations and alignment with educational priorities are demonstrated (Ch. 4-6, 24, 106).
